transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-15 14:00 PST
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Carter (CTO), Marcus Hale (IT Security), Sofia Ruiz (ML Platform Lead), Tom Adler (Infra)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood. With me is Ravi, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Emily: Hi Jordan, hey Ravi. Doing well thanks, busy end of quarter.
[00:09] Marcus: Morning. We'll try to be efficient, thanks for scheduling.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. The goal today is a high-level discovery 

— understand your on-prem, air-gapped constraints and see how Redwood's private offering could map. We can talk about dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs but sounds like you're leaning on air-gapped on-prem for compliance?
[00:25] Sofia: Correct. We have regulated clients in pharma and healthcare, so all inference has to run in our data centers, completely offline. No egress to cloud.
[00:31] Ravi: Understood. Can you walk us through your infra 
— GPUs, networking, how you handle firmware/patching?
[00:36] Tom: Sure. Current cluster is a mix 
— three racks of A100-ish nodes, about 24 GPUs total. We're running a custom kubernetes variant, air-gapped nodes, outbound connections blocked. Storage is NVMe-backed with an NFS overlay for some artifacts.
[00:48] Emily: We prefer a validated hardware BOM; procurement cycles are long. Also need to confirm that any software updates can be applied offline, via signed bundles 
— can't have auto-check-ins to public endpoints.
[00:59] Jordan: Yep, that's a typical ask. Redwood Private supports an offline updater mechanism 
— we package signed update bundles that can be delivered through your secure channels and validated against customer KMS/HSM.
[01:10] Marcus: Can you expand on the KMS integration? We use an HSM appliance for key storage and rotation.
[01:14] Ravi: Right, so our Private control plane can be configured to use customer-managed KMS endpoints. For air-gapped setups we support encrypted update packages signed with a Redwood key plus customer key verification. We also can integrate with PKCS#11-compatible HSMs for key wrapping.
[01:29] Marcus: PKCS what 
— sorry, I missed that 
— PKCS#11?
[01:31] Ravi: PKCS#11, yep. Sorry, some transcribe stuff earlier turned into PKS, but it's PKCS#11.
[01:36] Emily: Important for us is auditability 
— we need immutable audit logs of model updates, who initiated them, and retention for 7 years. Does Redwood produce those logs locally?
[01:44] Jordan: Yes, audit logs are produced in the private deployment and stored locally. We can export them to your SIEM; retention policies are configurable. For air-gapped setups we provide the capability to ship logs to your on-prem logging cluster.
[01:56] Sofia: How do you handle model onboarding? We have both open models and some internally fine-tuned models. We also need to perform validation and A/B comparisons before promoting a model to production.
[02:05] Ravi: Workflow is: import model artifact as a signed bundle, runtime runs a validation pass 
— inference smoke tests, perf benchmarks, and a quality check against provided eval sets. We support canary rollouts and manual promotion. In air-gapped mode the entire pipeline runs on your infra.
[02:18] Tom: And updates 
— can we do offline rollbacks if an update fails?
[02:20] Jordan: You get versioned model artifacts and rollout policies. Rollback is a supported operation; we can also keep a fallback model pinned to a lower-cost or lower-latency variant.
[02:30] Marcus: Latency is important. For diagnostic workflows we need p95 under 120ms for short prompts; for long batch scoring we want throughput with batching. How do you balance that?
[02:40] Ravi: Our runtime has continuous batching and KV cache features. For low-latency paths we route to a low-batch, high-priority lane. For batch scoring we use high-batch pools. On-prem you can allocate dedicated GPU pools per policy.
[02:51] Emily: Is that something we configure per model or per route?
[02:54] Ravi: Per route, per model 
— flexible routing policies.
[02:58] Sofia: A lot of this sounds promising. A practical concern: our models are LLaMA variants and some proprietary 8B and 30B fine-tunes. Do you support quantized runtimes and mixed precision to reduce memory footprint?
[03:09] Ravi: Yes, we support various quantization profiles and can recommend kernelized optimizations based on model arch and sequence length. For 8B you can generally run int8, 30B may need 4-bit profiles plus sharding across GPUs. We'll include recommended configs in the BOM.
[03:22] Tom: Regarding network setup 
— we use strict VLAN segmentation and no DNS to outside. How does Redwood handle downloads of model artifacts or container images?
[03:30] Jordan: For air-gapped installs we provide pre-packaged images and artifacts in tarballs. You ingest them via your secure transfer process (SCP, removable media, or SFTP via Jumpbox). Everything is signed and checksummed.
[03:43] Marcus: What about policy around PII data retention? We need controls to ensure request logs can be redacted and that embeddings or generated text aren't persisted beyond retention windows.
[03:52] Ravi: You can configure token-level logging and redaction rules. By default we store minimal telemetry locally; retention and redaction are configurable. For extra assurance we can run in a mode that only logs aggregated metrics, no raw prompts.
[04:04] Emily: Legal will want to see the security pack and our legal team will need to review data flow diagrams. Can you share those?
[04:10] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll send the standard security pack, SOC2 summary, pen test highlights, and a diagram tailored to on-prem air-gapped deployments.
[04:18] Sofia: About model validation 
— we want to run a POC that includes our eval prompts and a gold set. Ideally we can run it side-by-side with our internal inference for a week and compare regression metrics. Is that feasible?
[04:28] Ravi: Yes, we typically run a POC where we deploy a 3-node cluster, ingest your models and eval sets, then run parallel inference to compare outputs, latency, and cost. We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet.
[04:38] Tom: BOM: procurement needs exact SKU suggestions. Can you recommend GPU counts, NVMe sizes, and network requirements for a 3-node starter?
[04:46] Ravi: For a starter we'd propose 3 nodes with 4xH100-equivalent GPUs per node or 8xA100 80GB per node depending on availability. NVMe 8TB per node for model cache plus at least 100Gb interconnect for cross-GPU transfers. We'll include alternatives 
— lower-cost profiles using 4-bit quantization with more GPUs.
[05:02] Emily: Do you support FIPS-compliant builds?
[05:05] Jordan: We have options for FIPS/TLS stacks and can work with your security team on the compliance checklist. For full FIPS it may require some additional validation steps.
[05:14] Marcus: Okay, how about maintenance windows? Our change control only allows monthly maintenance. Can Redwood support manual update windows and static scheduling?
[05:22] Ravi: Yes, updates are manual by default for air-gapped. You control when to apply bundles. We also support scheduling with your change control process.
[05:29] Sofia: Any objections or red flags on our side? I mean, cost is a factor 
— our finance team will want to see TCO vs running in-cloud. Do you provide cost modeling?
[05:39] Jordan: We can provide an initial TCO model factoring hardware, licensing, and operator time. For many regulated customers the compliance delta justifies on-prem. We'll include a cost matrix in the follow-up.
[05:48] Tom: On the network side, we'll need to confirm that the control plane components can be hosted inside our management subnet. Does Redwood need an external control plane?
[05:55] Ravi: For Private deployments the control plane can be customer-hosted or we can provide a local control plane with no external dependencies. For air-gapped 
— everything stays local.
[06:05] Emily: Good. For sign-off: legal and procurement will want the security pack, BOM, pricing, and a POC scope. Does that align with Redwood's next steps?
[06:12] Jordan: Yes. Immediate next steps from our side: send security pack and SOC2 highlights, draft BOM and recommended SKUs, propose POC scope and pricing. From yours: share model artifacts sizes and eval sets, and provide a couple of dates for the POC scoping call.
[06:25] Marcus: We'll try to get model sizes and sample eval sets to you by EOD Friday.
[06:29] Sofia: One more quick question 
— do you have experience with offline vulnerability scanning or SBOMs for the images?
[06:34] Ravi: We produce SBOMs and can run container image scans; for air-gapped we provide the SBOM and scan reports as artifacts.
[06:42] Jordan: Okay, I know we're close on time. Any final questions?
[06:46] Emily: No, this was very helpful. Appreciate the detail.
[06:49] Marcus: Same. We'll look for the docs.
[06:52] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pack and schedule the scoping call for the week of 12/22.
[06:58] Sofia: Thanks all.
[06:59] Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hears (PKCS#11 transcribed as PKS earlier). Some speaker label confusion at times in the original recording; cleaned minimally for clarity.
